source_text: Ἰγνάτιος, ὁ καὶ Θεοφόρος, τῇ εὐλογημένῃ ἐν χάριτι θεοῦ πατρὸς ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ τῷ σωτῆρι ἡμῶν, ἐν ᾧ ἀσπάζομαι τὴν ἐκκλησίαν τὴν οὖσαν ἐν Μαγνησίᾳ τῇ πρὸς Μαιάνδρῳ καὶ εὔχομαι ἐν θεῷ πατρὶ καῖ ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ πλεῖστα χαίρειν.
thought_title: Greeting to the Church in Magnesia
orientation: Ignatius opens his letter to the church in Magnesia with a formal greeting, identifying himself and blessing the church in the name of God the Father and Jesus Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Ignatius, the [one] also [called] God-bearer, to the [church] blessed in [the] grace of God [the] Father in Christ Jesus our Savior, in whom I greet the church that is in Magnesia near [the] Maeander and I pray in God [the] Father and in Jesus Christ [for] very many [greetings] to rejoice.

choices.why: The epithet is a title Ignatius uses for himself; rendering it literally preserves the wordplay and self-designation.
The perfect passive participle indicates a state of having been blessed, which the simple adjective captures.
The standard epistolary greeting formula; keeping the infinitive 'to rejoice' preserves the Greek idiom.
The relative pronoun refers to Christ Jesus, and the prepositional phrase indicates the sphere in which the greeting occurs.

pass_b_english: Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus, to the church at Magnesia on the Maeander, blessed in the grace of God the Father in Christ Jesus our Savior. In him I greet this church, and I pray that it may have abundant joy in God the Father and in Jesus Christ.

problems.why: Title for Ignatius vs. description of Ephesians; reader may conflate the two uses.
problems.fix: Capitalize 'God-Bearer' as Ignatius's title; lowercase the plural for the Ephesians.

fixed: Capitalized 'God-Bearer' as Ignatius's title; the plural for the Ephesians is not in this section.

problems.why: Capitalization varies for the same title; readers may miss that it is the same designation.

fixed: Standardized capitalization of 'God-bearer' to lowercase 'b' throughout.

problems.why: Title 'God-bearer'/'God-Bearer' vs. plural 'God-bearers' as description of believers; inconsistent capitalization.
problems.fix: Standardize capitalization and clarify when descriptive.

fixed: Capitalized 'God-Bearer' as a title for Ignatius, consistent with the glossary's treatment of divine names and titles.

problems.why: Lowercase 'God-bearers' as description of believers may seem unrelated to Ignatius's epithet.
problems.fix: Consider 'god-bearers' for believers to distinguish from Ignatius's title.

problems.why: Same title applied to Ignatius and to Ephesians; plural form may confuse.
problems.fix: Capitalize for Ignatius; lowercase or gloss for the Ephesians.

fixed: The confirmed problems refer to 'God-bearers' in the plural, but the English text here has 'God-Bearer' in the singular as Ignatius's epithet. The source has Θεοφόρος (God-bearer) as Ignatius's title. The checkers' suggestions about plural 'God-bearers' do not apply to this passage. The English already matches the source: Ignatius is called God-Bearer. No change is needed for the singular epithet. The plural issue is not present in this section.

polish.changed: Clarified that the greeting and prayer both address the same Magnesian church, unified the epithet 'God-bearer,' and smoothed the sentence flow for modern readers.

notes.why: Same epithet rendered four ways; reader may think these are different titles or people.
notes.fix: Standardize to one spelling, note 'Theophorus' as Greek equivalent.

notes.quote: Ignatius, who is also called Theophorus
notes.why: Same Greek title, one translated and one transliterated; reader may think they differ.
notes.fix: Use 'God-Bearer (Theophorus)' consistently or translate both the same way.

polish.changed: Standardized the title Theophorus, clarified the greeting flows through Christ, and smoothed the sentence rhythm for reading aloud.

notes.why: Same Greek title (Theophorus) rendered three ways; reader may miss connection.
Same Greek title (Theophoros) applied to Ignatius and to Ephesians; reader may miss the echo.
notes.fix: Note that 'bearers of God' echoes Ignatius's own title.
